payload.description:
## Trigger
The owner reports slow basicly work, especially with Codex, and requests a full harness redesign proposal before implementation.

## Success Criteria
One coherent task owner by default; justified independent review and selective delegation; every agent, skill and projected instruction audited; lean contextual guidance and useful deterministic automation; preserved fast board and tracker; measured end-to-end improvements without correctness or safety regression.

## Authorization
Only planning, worktree provisioning and persistent backlog creation are approved now. Do not create a Codex goal, dispatch implementation, run paid evaluation trials, or change product behavior until the owner approves this backlog, the goal is then created, and the owner sets it in Codex. All proposed children remain deferred and labelled awaiting-user-approval. Existing independently authorized sessions retain their own scope.

## Design position
Optimization is measured improvement, not a promise of perfection or a universal two-times speedup. Retain useful controls. Convert roles to skills only when context and permissions permit. Use references for selectively loaded details and scripts only where existing commands do not already supply reliable behavior. Remove redundant handovers while preserving recovery and accountability.

## Coordination
Work on an isolated harness-redesign-plan worktree. The tracker remains repository-wide. Reconcile with basicly-h79lott and existing board, tracker and eval work. Do not claim, modify or duplicate the active basicly-bl1y0ii and basicly-g5ic8mo scopes.

## Demonstration
After approval, run matched repeated task evaluations and real board/tracker consumer journeys, report quality, elapsed time, token cost, repairs and interventions.

Follow current primary-source skill guidance with selective references and deterministic scripts where justified.

payload.text: Research baseline verified 2026-10-26: Anthropic https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-agents-when-to-fold-subagents-into-your-main-agent-loop supports conditional consolidation, not universal 2x speed; reported one customer runtime and one shipping-step regression in two trials. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents recommends main-context work for tightly coupled phases and isolated agents for self-contained/noisy/restricted work. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices supports independent fresh-context review but warns about invented findings. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents and https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills support selective delegation and progressive disclosure. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latency-optimization prioritizes fewer sequential calls, less generated output, parallel tools and deterministic operations. Builder evidence: https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering and https://www.langchain.com/blog/tuning-deep-agents-different-models support trace-driven and family-specific optimization; https://mariozechner.at/posts/2025-11-30-pi-coding-agent/ supplies minimal-harness experience; https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases is a parallelism counterexample with correctness tradeoffs unsuitable for silently importing here. These are evidence and hypotheses, not recommendations to adopt dependencies. Refresh model-specific guidance before implementation.

Adversarial review of the owner request: retain the board and tracker as explicit product requirements. Replace perfect optimization with measurable latency, quality, cost and usability objectives. Convert subagents to skills only when isolation, tool enforcement and independent judgment are unnecessary; avoid one skill per former persona. Keep a dedicated fresh-context review boundary until controlled tests show a better alternative. references/ is for selective detail, not empty directories or indirection for short skills; follow https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, with the current cli-tools skill as a local example. Scripts must save repeated reasoning or improve deterministic correctness, preferably reusing existing CLI commands; delete only with caller and consumer evidence. Remove redundant handovers, not crash recovery or accountability. Do not equate fewer tokens or fewer agents with faster correct completion. Live board activity must distinguish unavailable telemetry from idleness. Audit every skill source and effective output, including unselected technology skills; this full audit is proposed, not completed by this planning turn.

## Trigger
When basicly work is slow, especially with Codex, I want a measured redesign of the complete harness, so I can finish correct work faster while keeping a clear board and durable backlog.

## Success Criteria
One coherent task owner by default; justified independent review and selective delegation; every agent, skill and projected instruction audited; lean contextual guidance and useful deterministic automation; preserved fast board and tracker; measured end-to-end improvements without correctness or safety regression.

## Authorization
Only planning, worktree provisioning and persistent backlog creation are approved now. Do not create a Codex goal, dispatch implementation, run paid evaluation trials, or change product behavior until the owner approves this backlog, the goal is then created, and the owner sets it in Codex. All proposed children remain deferred and labelled awaiting-user-approval. Existing independently authorized sessions retain their own scope.

## Design position
Optimization is measured improvement, not a promise of perfection or a universal two-times speedup. Retain useful controls. Convert roles to skills only when context and permissions permit. Use references for selectively loaded details and scripts only where existing commands do not already supply reliable behavior. Remove redundant handovers while preserving recovery and accountability.

## Coordination
Work on an isolated harness-redesign-plan worktree. The tracker remains repository-wide. Reconcile with basicly-h79lott and existing board, tracker and eval work. Do not claim, modify or duplicate the active basicly-bl1y0ii and basicly-g5ic8mo scopes.

## Demonstration
After approval, run matched repeated task evaluations and real board/tracker consumer journeys, report quality, elapsed time, token cost, repairs and interventions.
